constraints: Fallback is optional: a patient may have no formal Picked, Possible, or Fallback-Possible result.
Fallback must pass an answer-blind evidence floor based on clinical tier, compatible specimen, rankable QC, within-test rank, and family guardrails.
Unmapped and commensal/endogenous families remain Audit or Context and cannot become Fallback-Possible.
A Level 4 hospital-only Context candidate remains visible to clinicians but cannot become Fallback-Possible.
Missing evidence is unknown rather than negative; abstention means insufficient positive evidence, not absence of infection.
The policy is answer blind; benchmark answers are used only by a separate post-hoc evaluator.
